ITEM 2 - SHARE THE BARE-REPO RECIPE, AND IT IS NOT A DIRECT CALL (DoD 2).

`createDeploymentImageBuilder` CANNOT simply call `extractCommittedPath`. The helper removes its temporary bare repo in a `finally` before returning, while the builder must hand that directory to `archiveIntoDocker` and needs it ALIVE until docker has consumed it. Wiring the call directly typechecks green and builds against a deleted directory.

EXTRACT THE SHARED PRIMITIVE INSTEAD. Exactly this much is duplicated: verify `<sha>^{commit}` via rev-parse; resolve `--git-path objects` to an absolute path and reject CR/LF/NUL in it; `mkdtempSync` under `tmpdir()`; `git init --bare --template= --object-format=<sha1|sha256>`; write `objects/info/alternates`. Give it a shape whose CALLER owns teardown - either return the directory and let the caller run the prefix-fenced `rmSync`, or take a callback and tear down around it. Then `extractCommittedPath` composes it and adds its `--show-toplevel` check plus the checkout; the builder composes it and adds the docker archive.

DECIDE THE `core.autocrlf=false` QUESTION DELIBERATELY. The helper's `GIT` array carries it and the builder's does not. Whichever way the shared primitive goes, that flag starts applying to a path it did not before or stops applying to one it did. Say in the completion record whether the helper's stated reasoning transfers to an image archive, and which behaviour you chose.

THE FOUR ARMS IN deploy-image-build.test.ts MUST PASS UNEDITED, including :20 "despite dirty files". That file is NOT an owned path. If a change makes an arm fail, the fold changed the builder's behaviour - fix the fold, do not touch the arm.

implementationPlan.note:
ITEM 2 DONE — one shared primitive, caller-owned teardown, four arms UNEDITED and passing, and the archived bytes proved byte-identical.

THE PRIMITIVE: `withBareSourceRepository<T>(git, {repository, sha}, hooks)` in git-source-extract.ts. `T` is the CALLER's own result type, so neither caller translates a foreign refusal. Hooks: `prefix` (mkdtemp prefix, kept per-caller so a leaked directory still names its seam), `refuse()` (unverifiable commit / unusable object store / failed bare init), optional `precondition()` and `use(directory)`. It owns exactly the duplicated span the step enumerated — rev-parse `<sha>^{commit}` with stdout equality, `--git-path objects` with CR/LF/NUL rejection, mkdtemp under tmpdir, `init --bare --template= --object-format=`, the alternates write — and the prefix-fenced `rmSync` in a `finally` AROUND `use`, which is the point: the builder streams `git archive` into Docker's stdin from that directory, so a helper that removed it before returning would typecheck green and archive nothing. It deliberately does NOT catch: each caller keeps its own catch and vocabulary, while the `finally` still fires, so a throwing `use` cannot leak either.

WHY `precondition` EXISTS rather than moving the check: `extractCommittedPath`'s `--show-toplevel` refusal sat BETWEEN the commit verify and the objects resolution. Folding without the hook would have reordered it after the objects resolution and mkdtemp, flipping which refusal wins when a bad sha and a subdirectory workspace are both present (SOURCE_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE would have become SOURCE_PATH_UNAVAILABLE). The hook keeps both callers' refusal ORDER byte-for-byte what it was.

THE `core.autocrlf=false` DECISION, made deliberately: the shared primitive CARRIES the flag; the builder's `git archive` keeps this module's OWN flag array WITHOUT it. The helper's stated reasoning — "a host with the global flag on would otherwise hand the migration tool CRLF bytes the commit does not contain" — does NOT transfer to an image archive, because the primitive runs only `rev-parse` and `init --bare` for the builder and neither converts content. I did not assume that; I measured it two ways.
  (1) `git -c core.autocrlf=false init --bare --template= --object-format=sha1 .` writes a config containing only repositoryformatversion/filemode/bare/symlinks/ignorecase, and `git config --local --get core.autocrlf` in that repo exits 1. The `-c` override is NOT persisted, so the archive spawned in that directory cannot inherit it.
  (2) A THROWAWAY BYTE-EQUALITY PROBE (apps/daemon/fold-probe-77207fb3.test.ts, run then deleted; kept OUT of src so no peer's scoped `src` leg could pick it up). It hand-rolled HEAD's exact pre-fold recipe with HEAD's flag array, archived, and SHA256-compared against the folded builder's captured tar, over a repository holding a CRLF+LF text file and a NUL-bearing binary, at three source-repo settings:
      core.autocrlf=false  sha256 baf21d2086340b74f180434e23e81d4df965c7e1ec5d75e71b5a124a1b680556  10240 bytes
      core.autocrlf=true   sha256 a89c0b7a5957f4e0d17119340083001d0577e265469caedc4b9828a14abceee3  10240 bytes
      core.autocrlf=input  sha256 a89c0b7a5957f4e0d17119340083001d0577e265469caedc4b9828a14abceee3  10240 bytes
    before == after in all three. (The false-vs-true hash difference is what was COMMITTED under each setting, not anything the fold did — each row compares pre-fold to post-fold at the SAME setting.) That answers the step's adversarial question directly: the four arms would pass either way because the arm's binary carries a NUL, so I did not rely on them for this.
